title: Improved Regularization of Convolutional Neural Networks with Cutout
notes: Close to an ideal case: a single-knob augmentation ablation, on CIFAR, with an official repository. Both arms are identical but for the augmentation, so the reduction is nearly free of judgement calls.

claims.text: Adding cutout augmentation lowers test error on CIFAR-10 compared to the same network trained without it.
claims.notes: The core claim, and the cleanest possible shape for reduced-scale testing.

claims.text: Cutout lowers test error on CIFAR-100 compared to the same network without it.
claims.notes: Same mechanism on a harder label set; still small enough to subsample.

claims.text: Cutout combines with existing data augmentation to give a further improvement, rather than substituting for it.
claims.notes: An interaction between two augmentations; resolving it needs more power than three seeds give.

claims.text: The optimal cutout patch size varies by dataset, and performance degrades if the patch is too large.
claims.notes: A trend over patch size with a clear turning point; three or four sizes make this visible.

claims.text: A WideResNet with cutout reaches 3.08% test error on CIFAR-10.
Cutout improves results on SVHN relative to the same network without it.
claims.notes: SVHN is much easier, so the reported gain is small and may not clear the noise at reduced scale.
